title: Apples and Bananas

scenario.title: Refactoring under tests
scenario.body: The book writes this program eight different ways, and the same tests keep every version honest. That only works if the tests ask the right questions. The book's replace() never sees the vowels in "crème brûlée" or "Éclair", and "-v O" is turned away for being a capital. Rewrite it however you like, as long as every test stays green.

character.name: Melody
character.role: a frog who sings with one vowel

tagline: Melody the frog knows one song: "I like to eat apples and bananas." Pick a vowel and Melody sings any words you give her with that vowel only. Oo-ploos ond bononos!

brain_blurbs.book: Swaps a, e, i, o and u.
brain_blurbs.real: Swaps accented vowels too, like é and û, and doesn't mind a capital vowel.

rules.test_usage: Explains herself when you ask for help
rules.test_bad_vowel: X isn't a vowel, so Melody says no
rules.test_accented_vowels: é, è and û are vowels too: "Crème brûlée" becomes "Crama bralaa"
rules.test_accents_typed_as_two_pieces: An accent typed as a separate piece still counts
rules.test_capital_vowel_option: Picking a capital O works as well as a small o
rules.test_still_rejects_non_vowels: A capital X still isn't a vowel
rules.test_only_vowels_change: Everything that isn't a vowel stays put (y too)
rules.test_singing_twice: Singing the song twice gives the same song
